claim: deploy.yml (Deploy to Production)'s workflow_run trigger acts only on this repository's own CI runs on main -- a push, or a manual (workflow_dispatch) run -- as far as a strict text reader can hold it (a direct, writer-only workflow_dispatch of deploy.yml itself runs the stages too, as before). ci-gate carries no job-level if (plain, quoted or spaced key) and one refusal step equal, line for line, to the allowed text: it reads the triggering run's event and head repository through env and exits 1 unless the event is 'push' or 'workflow_dispatch' and the repository is this one (a dispatch from a fork is refused); no line of ci-gate names GITHUB_ENV or GITHUB_OUTPUT literally. The on: block, up to the next top-level key, equals the allowed one and no defaults: is set. The jobs: block holds only plain job keys (a quoted, flow-style, anchored or aliased job key, a job-level line that is not a plain lowercase key (quoted, tagged, anchored, explicit or merge key), a five-space indent, an unclosed quoted job-level value, a tab or a duplicate fails), the job set is fixed, and each job's single job-level if (block scalars read with their blank lines, plain scalars with their continuation lines) equals the one allowed: every workflow_run-startable job requires the own-run group (event push or workflow_dispatch, and this repository), rollback-guide is dispatch-only; no job is a reusable-workflow call; nothing sets continue-on-error. Held by scripts/check_deploy_own_pushes.py (gate-owned, run with python3 -I), whose --self-test plants exactly the 52 breaks it lists, including a fork's dispatch, another event type and a missing repository check in a stage if, in deploy-audit's if and in the refusal step; run by scripts/test_pr_audit_gate.py. Not held: how ci-gate executes -- the guard pins the refusal step's text and each job's if, so a job-level key other than if, another step or action before the refusal step, an env/path-file write other than the literal GITHUB_ENV/GITHUB_OUTPUT, or a column-0 comment inside on: hiding an added trigger can turn ci-gate green on a foreign run unnoticed (known examples, all passing: `concurrency: |` before the refusal step; container, runs-on: self-hosted or services on ci-gate; job-level env: BASH_ENV; a github-script step exporting BASH_ENV; a GITHUB_PATH or indirect env-file write; the on: comment); runtime still holds for each because every stage's and deploy-audit's if independently requires the own-run group, is pinned exactly, and none of these changes it, and deploy.yml is gate-owned (closing the class: tech-debt.d/2026-09-30-batch-open-prs-2026-09-29.md); ci-gate's first step (the conclusion check, pinned separately by ADR-0097's row) and GitHub's own YAML evaluation (a form this reader accepts but GitHub reads differently) (workflow_run runs main's copy, so the step first runs on the merge commit's Deploy run). Founder, 2026-09-30, on #534, verbatim picks: "Sign off, add deploy fix (Recommended)", "Yes, covered (Recommended)" (his sign-off covers the guard and this fragment, 33 gate-owned files), "Honest record (Recommended)" (this record names what the guard does not hold; he re-confirmed the sign-off on the files it changes) and "Also allow manual runs" (so pr_audit_gate.py's CI-side merge re-entry, a workflow_dispatch of CI on main, still reaches the deploy audit). Recorded as ADR 0097's 2026-09-30 amendment.
